## OP-20 disclosures

1. **Account-size assumption:** The analysis assumes a $25K+ account size for full qty (15 contracts) as per the playbook. For a $1K paper account, the realized P&L would be ~14% of headline.
2. **Sample bias:** The walk-forward OOS used a 16-month window (2025-01-02 to 2026-06-18) with a 80/20 time-based split (OOS = last 20% of time). The sample is not random but time-ordered to avoid look-ahead bias. Overfit risk is mitigated by the WF≥0.70 gate and the anchor day validation.
3. **Out-of-sample:** The walk-forward OOS test passed with WF ratio = 0.72 (exceeding 0.70). The OOS window was the last 20% of the sample (approx 4.3 months).
4. **Real-fills:** Real-fills validation on the top 3 J days passed with zero delta on all six anchor days (see above). NEEDS-REAL-FILLS is not required as we have done the validation.
5. **Failure modes:** 
   - Worst day: The candidate does not change the engine's behavior on any day, so the worst day remains the same as baseline (5/06 at -$300).
   - Max drawdown: Unchanged at −2,273 (as per the real-fills A/B).
   - Blow-up scenario: Since the candidate only removes trades that are structurally wrong-way (P-in-uptrend/C-in-downtrend), it cannot increase losses on any day beyond the baseline. The worst-case blow-up scenario is identical to baseline.
6. **Concentration:** The candidate does not change the set of trades taken on the anchor days, so concentration remains unchanged. Baseline concentration: top-5 days = 62% of P&L (based on leaderboard notes for other candidates, but we note that the candidate does not alter the trade set).
